name: Mission San Xavier del Bac
aka: The White Dove of the Desert

dates.altered: Extensive repair to church and convento in 1906 by Bishop Granjon of Tucson; the survey says that except for the facade and doorway 'the whole structure was restored' then, and that the east tower has never been finished.
dates.note: The survey prints 'Date of Erection; 1797'; the Wikipedia infobox prints 'current structure dates to 1783–1797'; the style node gives 1797. The survey's 1797 is the completion date and the infobox's span the construction period, so they are not in disagreement.

quotes.text: The beautifully proportioned dome climaxing the exterior as well as the interior of the structure, and the vaults are constructed of brick They were built, without forms or centering, by pro- jecting each succeeding header course in an aroh or fan shaped form of construction, and were backed up with a rubble masonry fill ■where floors occurred over vaults.

quotes.text: Between the two flanking towers is the facade which remains com- pletely untouched since the day the finishing touches were put on it in 1797 Made entirely of baked adobe clay, the design is a curious one and the detail of the ornamentation is rather crude, nevertheless, it is considered one of the most beautiful things of its kind

note: Seeded 4 Sep 2026. The survey confirms the node's own note in its own words: fired ('burned adobe') brick throughout, plastered, with brick dome and vaults built without centering -- the one borderlands building that is not sun-dried earth. It states no overall dimension in the spans read.
